svg.text: Timing waterfall — two navigations, plotted against frames and clocks
The diagram this branch is actually about. Every constant is the real one from the source. The two traces use different horizontal scales — each has its own axis.

svg.text: 600 ms scroll-settle fallback armed — cancelled at scrollend
representative frames only; the browser paints every ~16.7 ms throughout

g.text: 1 Click on the next-phrase arrow.
2 step() advances pendingPhraseIndexRef synchronously; emitInternalFocus stamps the strip’s own marker.
3 Commit 1 — focus set; navigate internal stamps a nav marker and writes through to the host.
4 Commit 2 — echo adopted; consumeInternalNav true so the list does not fade; the strip updates its display ref at once.
5 The window-start guard runs and hands this run back: the focus moved, so the focus machinery owns the centring.
6 One rAF later, centerGroup smooth. That frame of delay lets the window slide settle, avoiding an overshoot-and-return.
7 The 600 ms fallback is armed alongside scrollend listeners on BOTH the clipping viewport and the content row.
8 The pitch sample is centred on the focus, so an ordinary step can move it far enough to re-derive the window half.
9 Commit 3 — renderWindowStart moves while the focus stays put.
10 The layout effect defers instead of centring: a glide is in flight, so it records windowChangedDuringScrollRef.
11 scrollend — adaptive to real hardware, no guessed duration. Cancels the fallback.
12 onSettled — apply the deferred correction, arm a hold, and only now commit the active segment.
13 The committed flip re-anchors synchronously before paint, then hands off to the hold.
14 Inactive link icons fade over 200 ms. Their layout space is reserved, so this corrects sub-pixel drift only.
15 The hold ticks every frame, then goes idle after 200 ms of quiet — keeping its observer connected.
16 The gloss placeholder resolving and the arc-settle pass widen content left of the focus, 300-500 ms in.
17 That reflow restarts the tick loop and re-centres. Without the surviving observer the focus stays stranded off-centre.
Off this scale: the nav marker’s 3000 ms TTL, armed at t=0, and the hold’s 2000 ms hard cap, landing at t≈2300.

svg.text: BookUSJ request in flight — unbounded, nothing backstops it
curtain down (opacity 0, dropped instantly at 0ms duration)

g.text: 1 Pick JHN 3:16 while looking at LUK. Host delivery 1.
2 RENDER PHASE — the book differs from displayedBookRef, so awaitingSettle and fadePhase out are set during this render.
3 Curtain to opacity 0 at transitionDuration 0ms. Instant, not gradual, because the old book leaves in this same commit.
4 The loader sees isCrossBookSwap, swaps in Loading, and unmounts the old book’s entire subtree.
5 Request in flight. This is the one span with no timer around it — a pending focus request is bounded by navigation, not a clock.
6 Duplicate-payload stabilisation, extract, tokenize, resegment. Main-thread work, and it scales with book size.
7 Commit — Interlinearizer mounts keyed on the book; the window is built centred; needsInitialSnap is true (anchor is mid-book).
8 The layout effect snaps the verse to the top before paint, so the new book never paints at scrollTop 0.
9 First paint of the new book — entirely behind the curtain.
10 rAF re-snap, now measuring against real painted geometry.
11 Quiet timer (100 ms) and deadline backstop (500 ms) both armed.
12 Arc-measurement waves. Each relayResize re-snaps and re-arms the quiet timer, so settled is reported only once they stop.
13 The quiet window finally runs to completion, ahead of the deadline.
14 reportSettled — fadePhase in, plus a 500 ms timer down to idle.
15 Curtain rises on the shared recenter clock.
16 Host delivery 2, the precise target, arriving mid-reveal. One picker selection, two navigations.
17 Re-engage — clear the fade-in timer, awaitingSettle true, fadePhase out. The curtain lifts once, on the next settle.
18 The strip’s fresh mount takes the instant-jump path and holds centred through the reveal.

svg.text: What the two traces say together

g.text: Nothing here is on a single clock. Trace A alone runs five: one rAF of deferral, a 200 ms slot transition, a 200 ms quiet window, a 600 ms scrollend
fallback, a 2000 ms hold cap, and a 3000 ms marker TTL. Each exists because a different actor finishes at a time nobody can predict.
The dominant reflow lands after the quiet window lapses. That single fact is why the hold’s observer outlives its tick loop, and why the settle is
event-driven rather than a per-frame poll. Read left to right on the holdCentered lane of trace A: idle, then alive again 350 ms later.
Prefer real signals over guessed durations. scrollend beats a timeout; a ResizeObserver wave beats a poll; a quiet-debounce beats a fixed wait. Every
timer on these lanes is a backstop for a signal that may not arrive — never the primary mechanism. Both the 600 ms fallback and the 500 ms deadline go unused here.
The load span is the only unbounded one. Everything else is capped. That asymmetry is why a book change is bounded by navigation rather than by a
clock: a request that never returns strands nothing, because the user leaving the book is what abandons it.
One user action, two navigations. Trace B’s dots 1 and 16 are the same click. Any code that assumes a picker selection arrives once is wrong.
